Thanks again for the call yesterday — great to learn more about Zenify's inference mix (long chat flows + low-latency scoring). - Cluster options A/B/C (balanced, high-throughput, low-latency) with example min-GPU baselines.
- Standard ramp windows (30/60/90 days) and optional burst capacity windows for traffic spikes.
- Pilot path: 30-day proof-of-performance using dedicated lanes + host fallback.

Attachments: dedicated-options-v1.pdf (6 pages)

1) Lowest 95th percentile latency at peak
2) Predictable unit cost (flat monthly commit)
3) Fast time-to-scale with auto-burst enabled

If you confirm #1–#3 I'll loop in our infra pricing lead (Ben) and infra architect (Karthik) with the exact GPU counts and a ramp table that fits your Q4 forecast.

Available for a quick follow-up tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Naomi / Ben — ran the numbers and sketched an activation ladder. Attachment: gpu-slate-matrix.xlsx (sheet: ZenifySizing)

Summary (assumptions):
- Short-chat model: 128 tokens, optimized kernels, single-GPU can serve ~180 qps at 150ms median under batching=8, continuous KV cache enabled.
- Long-context summarizer: 4k tokens, realistically 6–10 qps per GPU at target 500ms median when using quantized 4-bit runtime and large KV segments.

Proposed configs (min GPUs / typical steady throughput / ramp):
A) Sprint (latency-first): min 12 GPUs (8 A100-equivalent serving + 4 for long-context batches). Baseline approx: short-chat 1,400 qps, long-context 40 qps. Ramp 30 days: 25% -> 60% -> 100%.
B) Balanced (cost & perf): min 8 GPUs (6 + 2). Baseline: short-chat 900 qps, long-context 25 qps. Ramp 45 days: 20% -> 50% -> 100%.
C) Conservative (cost-smoothing): min 6 GPUs (4 + 2) + burst pool on request. Baseline: short-chat 650 qps, long-context 16 qps. Ramp 90 days: 10% -> 35% -> 100%.

Fallback policy: auto-fallback to hosted compatible variant with 200ms extra P95 latency and temporary burst credits. We recommend keeping soft-burst enabled for first 60 days to avoid immediate decommit.

Pilot path: start with config B as a pilot for 30 days (scale to 40% of predicted peak) to validate latency; if metrics hit 95th/median targets, convert to chosen commit (A/B/C).

Notes for Ben: I left conservative burst sizing in the spreadsheet and a column for estimated warmup hours needed for each pod type.

Karthik

Liam / procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. See below a short, actionable summary and next steps (we kept costs high-level here; Ben will send line items in a separate email).

Recommended path (our suggestion):
- Start with Balanced config (Option B) as a 30-day pilot at 40% of forecasted peak to validate latency targets.
- If pilot metrics meet SLA (150ms median short-chat, 500ms median long-context) by day 21, sign up for a 12-month commit using Option B with a 45-day ramp to full capacity.
- If Zenify prioritizes absolute latency during Q4 promotions, choose Option A with 30-day ramp instead.

Rollbacks / pilot exit:
- Pilot includes an escape hatch — if 3-day rolling median fails SLA after day 21, we will automatically scale down to a conservative config and pause the commit conversion; Zenify pays only pilot usage and any consumed burst credits.

Attachments we will deliver: SOW-dedicated-zenify-draft.docx (initial SOW for pilot + conversion language)

Action items:
1) Procurement: review SOW and return commercial redlines (we will send line-item pricing separately).
2) Zenify infra: confirm whether KV cache is acceptable for long-context (Karthik assumed yes).
3) Naomi: schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff next week to lock pilot parameters.

Proposed kickoff: Wed Oct 08, 2025 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

If that looks good I'll circulate the SOW and Ben's pricing lines for procurement review.
